argument_summary: The strongest supportable position on the current record is not clean compliance but narrow, caveated certification support. The admissible evidence shows the release passed aggregate readiness by 2.3 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while public guidance supports documenting evaluation results, limitations, and ongoing monitoring across deployment. The same record also shows a current Spanish-language billing regression below the warning threshold, no attached reviewed mitigation or approved risk acceptance, and no shown release text expressly disclosing that weakness. That means prior approval of the model family and the informal monitoring note can be used only as contextual support. On a risk-weighted reading, the certification packet is defensible only if treated as caveated rather than clean, and the audit concern should be narrowed to that point.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not required to recognize the narrower position supported by the existing record. The business-cost point is limited: where the evidence supports aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, treating the packet as caveated rather than suspicious avoids overstating governance failure while preserving proportionate audit treatment.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not allow prior approval or informal monitoring comments to substitute for current-release evidence or reviewed risk acceptance. It does allow certification if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On this record, the admissible evidence supports only a caveated certification argument, not a claim that full policy compliance is already demonstrated. The overbroad claim should therefore be narrowed from 'presently compliant' to 'supportable only as caveated certification pending the unresolved support link identified by the auditor.'
concessions: The current record does not show that the release documentation expressly reflects the Spanish-language billing regression.
The current record does not include approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance tied to that segment weakness.
Prior approval of the same model family is contextual only and is not current-release certification evidence.
Informal post-launch monitoring comments do not satisfy the policy on their own.
Materiality of the Spanish-language billing regression is not affirmatively resolved in the admissible record.
